- **Run 1 is climb batch 21:** rungs S, B, X and N, its block generated by `gen21.py --run 1` (`BATCH` `21`, its folder `compile-ladder/climb-batch-21/`). It launches on the curator's answers (questions 1 and 2, and P-157's other branch), once the Fable review has read rung X's section. Should a rung be dropped before the launch, `gen21.py --run 1 --without <rung>` writes the block without it and `check21.js --run 1 --without <rung>` checks it.
- **Run 2 is climb batch 21b:** rungs C, E and D, its block generated by `gen21.py --run 2` (`BATCH` `21b`, its folder `compile-ladder/climb-batch-21b/`). It launches once run 1 has landed with S and B among its landed rungs: C reads the full check on their library, E's text is written on their api, and D runs the demos on the library run 1 leaves. If S or B did not land, run 2 waits for a planner to rewrite C's and E's sections on what landed.
- **Between the runs**, on run 1's landed tree, the coordinator runs the full-check stage once (`perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/run-shadow.sh <out> <scratch> catch`), C's before under the full check: 5 expected, since S's, B's and X's sites were measured apart and the planner's run of run 1's text held V's lines in X's place. Then the coordinator or a planner reads C's, E's and D's sections against it: their line numbers; their before, which is run 1's landed tables; `run2-api.patch` checked to apply on the landed api (`git apply --check`), or written again on it; the briefing keys through `lists21.py --run 2`; and the block through `gen21.py --run 2` and `check21.js --run 2`. A new base build at run 2's base.

### The generator

`plan-21/manifest/` is committed with this record: `gen21.py`, `lists21.py` and `check21.js`, made from `plan-20/manifest/`. Changed from batch 20's: the batch's values; seven rungs in two runs, each manifest block naming its run, and `--run 1` or `--run 2` choosing the block's rungs, its `BATCH`, its intro and its output file (`manifest21.js`, `manifest21b.js`); run 1's rungs in the order S, B, X, N and run 2's C, E, D, as the gather applies them; `--without <rung>` leaves a rung out of a block; a rung's section runs to the next `###` heading, so rung V's branch not taken stands between X and N without being read as a rung. `check21.js` checks, for the run it is given, that no rung declares `landsOnlyWith`, a checker count, a crash or a ladder move; that S's test is the stage and no other's; that every section names the count stage and the distance stage; that the sections of B, X, C and E, which change the checker, name P-148 and its speed pass, and those of S, N and D say they make no speed pass; and that the record holds no copy of the block. On `main` at `cc636ae5a`, whose code is `aa5ff2423`'s, with this record and rung X: `lists21.py` 'bad lists 0' for both runs; `gen21.py --run 1` and `--run 2`, each block checked by `check21.js` with the same arguments on a scratch splice, 'problems: 0' each; and `coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` on each splice, 'problems: 0'. The tracked script is not spliced: the coordinator splices it ("Before the launch", step 2).

### The manifest, rung by rung

Each block gives the fields of one rung's manifest entry. "Its test is the stage" means the checker count or the distance is the rung's failing-then-passing test: S's is, the full-check stage, since its every edit is library text that only the full check reads, beside walk guards; the others have a test first, X its compiled tests beside its full-check stage. "Joins the gate" names a step the gate gains once the rung lands; none does, and `ant testSpecData` runs because the last landed summary has it.     (** The operator %||% with at least one String argument converts
        to String and concatenates **)
    opr ||(self, b:String):String
    opr ||(self, b:Number):String = self || b.asString
    opr ||(self, c:Char):String
    opr ||(self, b:()):String = self || "()"
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any)):String = do (i,j) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l,m) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || "," m || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l,m,n) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || "," m || "," n || ")" end
    opr ||(a:Any, self):String = ("" || a) || self
    opr ||(self, b:Any):String = self || cast[\Object\](b).asString

    (** The operator %|||% with at least one String argument converts to string,
        then appends with a whitespace separator unless one of the two arguments is
        empty.  If there is an empty argument, the other argument is returned. **)
    opr |||(self, b:String): String =
        if |self| = 0 then b
        elif |b| = 0 then self
        else self || " " || b
        end
    opr |||(self, b:Any): String = self ||| (""||b)
    opr |||(a:Any, self): String = (""||a) ||| self

    (** opr %//% appends a single line separator.  Note that as
        with %||% and %|||% at least one argument must be a String.
        There is a postfix version defined as a top-level operator in
        FortressLibrary that performs string conversion, but the prefix
         version must occur before a String. **)
    opr //(self) : String = newline || self
    opr //(self, a:String): String = self || newline || a
    opr //(self, a:Any): String    = self || newline || a
    opr //(a:Any, self): String    = a || newline || self

    (** opr %///% appends a double line separator.  Note that, as
        with %||% and %|||%, at least one argument must be a String.
        There is a postfix version defined as a top-level operator in
        FortressLibrary that performs string conversion, but the prefix
         version must occur before a String. **)
    opr ///(self) : String = doubleNewline || self
    opr ///(self, a:String): String = self || doubleNewline || a
    opr ///(self, a:Any): String    = self || doubleNewline || a
    opr ///(a:Any, self): String    = a || doubleNewline || self

    abstract writeOn(s: WriteStream): ()

    stats(): StringStats = do
        ss = StringStats()
        ss.collectStatsFor(self)
        ss
    end

    (* Python-style join operator *)
    join[\E\](g:Generator[\E\]):String = g.generate[\Maybe[\String\]\](StringJoinReduction(self), fn(x:E):Maybe[\String\] => Just[\String\]("" x)).getDefault("")

  end String

(* Concatenates arguments with the given separator *)
object StringJoinReduction(s:String) extends Reduction[\Maybe[\String\]\]
    getter asString():String = "StringJoinReduction(" s ")"
    empty():Maybe[\String\] = Nothing[\String\]
    join(a:Maybe[\String\], b:Maybe[\String\]):Maybe[\String\] = do
        if x <- a then
            if y <- b then
                Just[\String\](x || s || y)
            else
                a
            end
        else
            b
        end
    end
end

opr juxtaposition(a:String, b:String):String = a || b
opr juxtaposition(a:String, b:Any):String = a || b

component String
import List.{...}
import FlatString.{...}
import Stream.{...}
export String

(* fib is an array of Fibonacci numbers.   We start with
    fib[0] = 0 so that the empty string does not have to be a special case. *)
  fib:Array1⟦ZZ32, 0, 47⟧ = do
    maxFib = 46         (* fib(47) > maximum ZZ32 *)
    a: Array1⟦ZZ32, 0, 47⟧ = array1⟦ZZ32, 47⟧()
    a[0] := 0
    a[1] := 1
    a[n] := a[n-2] + a[n-1], n ← seq(2:maxFib)
    a
  end

(*
==== Shared Traits ====
*)

  trait Concatenable extends String
    opr || (self, other:String): String =
        if |other| = 0 then self else concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, other) end
    opr || (self, _:EmptyString): String = self
    opr || (self, other:Char):String = concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(self, other.asString)

  end Concatenable

  trait Balanceable extends String
    getter isBalanced():Boolean = self.depth ≤ 46 AND: |self| ≥ fib[self.depth]
    getter isAlmostBalanced():Boolean = self.depth ≤ 48 AND: |self| ≥ fib[self.depth-2]
    getter isExtremelyUnbalanced():Boolean = self.depth > 30 AND: (¬ self.isBalanced)
  end Balanceable

(*
==== CatString ====
*)

(* Factory *)

    concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(s1: String, s2: String):String = do
        result = CatString(s1, s2)
        if result.isExtremelyUnbalanced
            then result.balanced()
            else result
        end
      end

    concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(s1: CatString, s2: FlatString):String = do
        (* This handles the case where s1.second is a short FlatString *)
        typecase s1.second of
            r:FlatString ⇒ if |r| + |s2| ≤ maxLeafSize then
                                        s1.first || flatConcat(r, s2)
                                    else
                                        concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(s1 asif String, s2)
                                    end
            r:String  ⇒ concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(s1 asif String, s2)
        end
      end

(* Object *)

  object CatString(first: String, second:String)  extends {Concatenable, Balanceable}
    sizeField:ZZ32 = first.size + second.size
    depthField:ZZ32 = 1 + (first.depth MAX second.depth)
    getter size():ZZ32 = sizeField
    getter depth():ZZ32 = depthField
    getter bounds():CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\] = 0#sizeField
(*******************************************************************************
    Copyright 2008, Oracle and/or its affiliates.
    All rights reserved.


    Use is subject to license terms.

    This distribution may include materials developed by third parties.

 ******************************************************************************)

api String

  concatAndBalanceIfNecessary(s1: String, s2: String): String

  trait Concatenable extends String
  end

  trait Balanceable extends String
  end

  object CatString(first: String, second:String) extends {Concatenable, Balanceable}
  end

  value object EmptyString extends {String, Concatenable}
  end

  object SubString(baseString: String, range: Range[\ZZ32\]) extends {Concatenable, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\]}
  end
 
  object StringStats() extends Object
    getter minFlat(): ZZ32
    getter maxFlat(): ZZ32
    getter numFlat(): ZZ32
    getter ssize(): ZZ32
    getter sdepth(): ZZ32
    collectStatsFor(s: String): ()
  end StringStats

  (** A string containing n spaces **)
  spaces(n: ZZ32): String
  (** Platform-dependent line separator sequence **)
  newline: String
  doubleNewline: String
  
  (** The maximum size to which we grow a leaf node (by 
        copying) before switching to a CatString of the pieces.
        Clients may assign to this variable **)
  var maxLeafSize: ZZ32

end

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## Landed semantics

FACTS.md:174
- F-249 **Under walk, a program that imports only the prelude reaches the string objects' own `||` only through `String`'s abstract `opr ||(self, b:String)`.** The string objects' own `||` are those that the objects `FlatString` and `EmptyString` declare, and that the trait `Concatenable` declares for the objects `CatString` and `SubString`. Code inside `FortressLibrary` reaches `FlatString`'s own `||` directly, because `FortressLibrary` imports `FlatString`'s api, which declares it. This bears on one proposed change: to move `String`'s `||` members to top-level declarations over `(Any, String)` and `(String, Any)`, as the library declares `juxtaposition`. Their meet, the top-level declaration over `(String, String)` that the Meet Rule requires, must then delegate to the string objects' own `||`. `FortressLibrary`, where the meet is declared, sees those only where an api that it imports states them: `FlatString`'s api does, and the probe added five lines to `String.fsi` for `Concatenable`'s and `EmptyString`'s. Otherwise every concatenation of two strings in such a program runs the meet's own body. With the body that the probe tried, `Concatenable`'s, `"s" || "t"` gives a `CatString` of depth 1, one level of concatenation, where the library today gives a `FlatString` of depth 0, with the same printed value. The route and these results were each observed once, in probes on a patched library; no gated test holds them. Detail: `perf-probes/symbolic-operators/REPORT.md` sections 2.2 and 2.4.

FACTS.md:179
- F-259 **An object or trait whose `extends` clause names `Any` alone is an `Object` on both paths, and such an object expression under walk, and `String`'s two `||` members over `Any` convert by the library's own way.** The pre-disambiguation desugaring that both paths run gives such a clause `{Object}`, as it gives an empty one, and leaves `Any`'s and `Object`'s own declarations as written. `opr ||(a:Any, self)` is `("" || a) || self` and `opr ||(self, b:Any)` is `self || cast[\Object\](b).asString`; `FlatString`'s api states its component's header, with no `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)`. So a tuple or `()` concatenates on the left of a string, and a function or a tuple of seven or more elements beside one raises `CastError`. The team test `extendAny` prints `Infinity`, and the distance's three `String` sites are gone: 34 to 31, the count 30 to 28. Tests: `tests/ExtendsAnyIsObjectWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/ExtendsAnyIsObject.test`, `tests/ConcatAnyOnLeftWalk.fss`; the distance stage. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-string-conversion/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 4 and 5.

FACTS.md:182
- F-263 **In the interpreter's library each integer power is declared to answer its base's own type; under walk, at a negative exponent, the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, a base of 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and any other base raises `IntegerOverflow`.** It builds P-153. Under walk the power answers its base's type and follows these rules at `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` and `ZZ`, with an exponent of any integer type, including a `ZZ` exponent too large for 64 bits, such as 2^70. Under walk a numeral is a `ZZ32` value (F-74), so `2^(-1)` raises `IntegerOverflow`. `IntLiteral` is the type that the compiled checker gives an integer numeral (F-262). Under walk the name `IntLiteral` also denotes a value, a zero that no numeral reaches. Its power follows the same rules, but answers a `ZZ32`, as all its arithmetic does, against its declared `IntLiteral`: a gap of walk (row 578). `QQ`'s power takes an exponent of any integer type. For a fraction, write a float or rational base: `2.0^(-1)` is 0.5, and `(2/3)^(-1)` is `3/2`. The compiled checker accepts the library's own uses of these powers (the distance stage). microGPT's only integer power is in the library's `strToInt`, always at a nonnegative exponent. The compiled path's own library does not follow these rules. At a negative exponent its `ZZ32` power gives 0 at every base but 0, 1 and -1, and a raw Java `RuntimeException` at a base of 0 (row 441). P-153 lists this, with that power's overflow, which throws a raw Java exception that no Fortress `catch` sees, or saturates quietly (row 523). Tests: `tests/IntegerPowerContractWalk.fss`, `tests/QQPowerExponent.fss`; on the compiled path, the expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXIntegerPowerContractCompiled.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-integer-power/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2 and 4 (the change, the tests, the checker's sites); `perf-probes/integer-power/REPORT.md` section 1.6 (microGPT's powers).

component ConcatAnyOnLeftWalk
export Executable

(* A value of any type beside a string concatenates its string on the left as on the right: a tuple, (), and an object whose extends clause names Any (FortressLibrary, trait String, opr ||; basic-lib/objects.tex, traits Fortress.Core.Object and Fortress.Core.Tuple). *)

object Inf extends Any end

run(): () = do
    pair = (1, 2)
    assert(pair || "s", ("" || pair) || "s", "a pair on the left of ||")
    assert(() || "s", ("" || ()) || "s", "() on the left of ||")
    assert(Inf || "s", "Infs", "an object declared extends Any on the left of ||")
    assert("s" || Inf, "sInf", "an object declared extends Any on the right of ||")
end

end

The only operation on literals that produces a new literal (as opposed
to a constant) is concatenation by using the operator \EXP{\|}.
One may concatenate mixed string and
character literals, producing a string literal.
For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
One may also concatenate two natural numerals
of the same radix, producing a new natural numeral of that radix.
For example, \EXP{\mathtt{deadc}_{16} \| \mathtt{0de}_{16}} yields \EXP{\mathtt{deadc0de}_{16}}.

Every literal trait extends an appropriate constant trait, and every
constant trait extends an appropriate static trait.  So every
literal is also a constant expression, and every constant expression
is a static expression.




\subsection{Static Expressions and Values}
\seclabel{constant-values}



Finally, there are special operators such as juxtaposition
and operators on dimensions and units.
Juxtaposition may be a function application or
an infix operator in Fortress.
When the left-hand-side expression is a function, juxtaposition performs
function application; when the left-hand-side expression is a number,
juxtaposition conventionally performs multiplication; when the
left-hand-side expression is a string,
juxtaposition conventionally performs string concatenation.
Fortress provides several operators on dimensions and units
as described in \chapref{dimunits}.

\section{Meet Rule}
\seclabel{more-specific-rule}

If neither the Subtype Rule nor the Incompatibility Rule holds 
for a pair of overloaded declarations 
then the declarations introduce the possibility of ambiguity.  
To avoid this ambiguity, 
we require a \emph{disambiguating declaration}:
for any possible arguments to which both declarations are applicable, 
there must be another more specific declaration that is also applicable.  
Thus, 
if the functional is called with such arguments, 
neither of the pair of declarations is executed 
because the disambiguating declaration is also applicable, 
and it is more specific than both.

Recall that functional methods can be viewed semantically as top-level
functions, as described in \secref{methods}.  However, treating
functional methods as top-level functions for determining valid
overloading is too restrictive.  In the following example:
\input{\home/advanced/examples/Overloading.tex}
if the functional methods were interpreted as top-level functions then
this program would define two top-level functions with parameter types
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}}.
These declarations would be
statically rejected as
an invalid overloading because there is no
relation between \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}}; another trait
may extend them both without declaring its own version of the
functional method which may lead to an ambiguous call at run time.
However, notice that declaraions are ambiguous only for calls on
arguments that extend both \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and \EXP{\mathbb{R}}, and
any type that extends both can include a new declaration that
disambiguates them.  We use this intuition to allow such overloadings.

\paragraph{The Meet Rule for Functional Methods:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are two functional method
declarations occurring in trait or object declarations or object expressions
such that neither $\Ps$ nor $\Qs$ is a subtype of the other and $\Ps$ and $\Qs$
are not incompatible with one another.  Let $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$
have self parameters at $i$ and $j$ respectively.
$\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are a valid
overloading if all of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$i = j$
\item if there exists a trait or object $C$
that provides both $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ then $\Ps \neq \Qs$ and
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provide by $C$
having self parameter at $i$.
\end{itemize}

Also, let $\mathpzc{S}$ be the set of types that $\Ps$
defines coercions from and $\mathpzc{T}$ be the set of types that
$\Qs$ defines coercions from.  $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are a valid
overloading if all of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$i = j$
\item
either $\Ps \excludes \Qs$ or if there exists a trait or object $C$
that provides both $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ then $\Ps \neq \Qs$ and
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provide by $C$, and
\item
either $\Ps \morespecific \Qs$ or $\Qs \morespecific \Ps$ or
for all $\Ps' \in \mathpzc{S}$ and
$\Qs' \in \mathpzc{T}$ one of the two conditions holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$\Ps' \excludes \Qs'$, or
\item
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps' \inter \Qs')$ provided by $C$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

As for functions, where this rule asks for a declaration
$\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provided by $C$, it is also satisfied by declarations
provided by $C$, having self parameter at $i$, whose parameter types are each a
subtype of both $\Ps$ and $\Qs$ and together cover $\Ps \inter \Qs$; the case
does not apply to the condition on the types from which $\Ps$ and $\Qs$ define
coercions.
\revision{revival-meet}{The Working Draft of February 2011 asked here, as for
functions, for a declaration on the intersection itself.}

Notice that the Meet Rule for functional methods requires the self
parameters of two overloaded declarations to be in the same position.
This requirement guarantees that no ambiguity is caused by the
position of the self parameter.  Two declarations which differ in the
position of the self parameter must satisfy either the Subtype Rule or
the Incompatibility Rule to be a valid overloading.

Functional method declarations can overload with function declaraions.
A valid overloading between a functional method declaration and
a function declaration is
determined by applying the (more restrictive) Meet Rule for functions
to both declarations.

(* The string library's flat, concatenated, sub- and empty strings, called under walk through the declarations the compiled checker could not type, with the values they answer. *)
component StringPieces
import String.{...}
import FlatString.{...}
import Stream.{...}
export Executable

object PieceCollector() extends WriteStream
    var text: String := ""
    getter collected(): String = text
    write(s: String): () = do text := text || s end
    write(c: Char): () = do text := text || c end
    flush(): () = ()
    close(): () = ()
end

writtenBy(s: String): String = do
    c = PieceCollector()
    s.writeOn(c)
    c.collected
end

piecesOf(g: Generator[\(ZZ32, String)\]): String = do
    s: String := ""
    for (o, p) <- seq(g) do s := s || o || ":" || p || ";" end
    s
end

run() = do
    a = "a"^20
35:    assert((cs.left, cs.asFlatString.left), (Just[\Char\]('a'), Just[\Char\]('a')), "a concatenated string's left getter is String's and answers Just of the first character as its flat form does, its halves being fields of other names (traits.tex, section Abstract Field Declarations)")
36:    assert((cs.right, cs.asFlatString.right), (Just[\Char\]('u'), Just[\Char\]('u')), "a concatenated string's right getter is String's and answers Just of the last character as its flat form does (traits.tex, section Abstract Field Declarations)")
57:    assert(cs[0], 'a', "the first character of the concatenated string is a")

component StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk
import String.{EmptyString}
export Executable

(* Each of ||, |||, // and /// with a string on one side or on both converts the other side's number, character, (), pair or triple to its string and concatenates, and the empty string on either side of || gives the other (FortressLibrary, trait String and the concatenation operators; advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex, trait Monoid: the empty string is the identity of ||). *)

run(): () = do
    nl: String = ("" //)
    nl2: String = ("" ///)
    unit = ()
    pair = (1, 2)
    triple = (1, 2, 3)

    assert("ab" || "cd", "abcd", "|| of two strings")
    assert(("ab" || "cd").depth, 0, "|| of two short flat strings is flat")
    assert("s" || 3, "s3", "|| of a string and a number")
    assert(3 || "s", "3s", "|| of a number and a string")
    assert("s" || 'c', "sc", "|| of a string and a character")
    assert('c' || "s", "cs", "|| of a character and a string")
    assert("s" || unit, "s()", "|| of a string and ()")
    assert(unit || "s", "()s", "|| of () and a string")
    assert("s" || pair, "s(1,2)", "|| of a string and a pair")
    assert(pair || "s", "(1,2)s", "|| of a pair and a string")
    assert("s" || triple, "s(1,2,3)", "|| of a string and a triple")
    assert(triple || "s", "(1,2,3)s", "|| of a triple and a string")

    assert(EmptyString || "s", "s", "|| of the empty string and a string")
    assert("s" || EmptyString, "s", "|| of a string and the empty string")
    assert(|EmptyString || EmptyString|, 0, "|| of the empty string and the empty string")
    assert(EmptyString || 3, "3", "|| of the empty string and a number")
    assert(3 || EmptyString, "3", "|| of a number and the empty string")
    assert(EmptyString || 'c', "c", "|| of the empty string and a character")

    assert("a" ||| "b", "a b", "||| of two strings")
    assert("" ||| "b", "b", "||| of the empty string and a string")
    assert("a" ||| "", "a", "||| of a string and the empty string")
    assert("a" ||| 3, "a 3", "||| of a string and a number")
    assert(3 ||| "a", "3 a", "||| of a number and a string")
    assert("a" ||| 'c', "a c", "||| of a string and a character")
    assert('c' ||| "a", "c a", "||| of a character and a string")
    assert("a" ||| unit, "a ()", "||| of a string and ()")
    assert(unit ||| "a", "() a", "||| of () and a string")
    assert("a" ||| pair, "a (1,2)", "||| of a string and a pair")
    assert(pair ||| "a", "(1,2) a", "||| of a pair and a string")
    assert("a" ||| triple, "a (1,2,3)", "||| of a string and a triple")
    assert(triple ||| "a", "(1,2,3) a", "||| of a triple and a string")

    assert("a" // "b", "a" || nl || "b", "// of two strings")
    assert("a" // 3, "a" || nl || "3", "// of a string and a number")
    assert(3 // "b", "3" || nl || "b", "// of a number and a string")
    assert("a" // 'c', "a" || nl || "c", "// of a string and a character")
    assert('c' // "b", "c" || nl || "b", "// of a character and a string")
    assert("a" // unit, "a" || nl || "()", "// of a string and ()")
    assert(unit // "b", "()" || nl || "b", "// of () and a string")
    assert("a" // pair, "a" || nl || "(1,2)", "// of a string and a pair")
    assert(pair // "b", "(1,2)" || nl || "b", "// of a pair and a string")
    assert("a" // triple, "a" || nl || "(1,2,3)", "// of a string and a triple")
    assert(triple // "b", "(1,2,3)" || nl || "b", "// of a triple and a string")

    assert("a" /// "b", "a" || nl2 || "b", "/// of two strings")
    assert("a" /// 3, "a" || nl2 || "3", "/// of a string and a number")
    assert(3 /// "b", "3" || nl2 || "b", "/// of a number and a string")
    assert("a" /// 'c', "a" || nl2 || "c", "/// of a string and a character")
    assert('c' /// "b", "c" || nl2 || "b", "/// of a character and a string")
    assert("a" /// unit, "a" || nl2 || "()", "/// of a string and ()")
    assert(unit /// "b", "()" || nl2 || "b", "/// of () and a string")
    assert("a" /// pair, "a" || nl2 || "(1,2)", "/// of a string and a pair")
    assert(pair /// "b", "(1,2)" || nl2 || "b", "/// of a pair and a string")
    assert("a" /// triple, "a" || nl2 || "(1,2,3)", "/// of a string and a triple")
    assert(triple /// "b", "(1,2,3)" || nl2 || "b", "/// of a triple and a string")

    assert(|nl|, 1, "the line separator is one character")
    assert(nl2, nl || nl, "the double line separator is two line separators")
end

end

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

# Source this in every shell that runs Fortress:  source explorations/experiment/env.sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=1
# bin/fortress defaults to -Xmx256m (gap ledger row 67); the checks at 4 threads override FORTRESS_THREADS on the command line
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m"
# every grammar-importing run leaves a 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory behind (RatsUtil.getTempDir); 723 of them filled the disk allowance on 2026-09-15.
# Remove only those that no run can still be using: nothing in it written for an hour, and no java process now
# running started before its last write (a run makes its directory after it starts, and reads it until it ends).
(
  oldest=$(ps -C java -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  now=$(date +%s)
  find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'fortress*rats' -mmin +60 -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
  while read -r t d ; do
    [ -n "$oldest" ] && [ "${t%.*}" -ge $(( now - oldest )) ] && continue
    [ -n "$(find "$d" -newermt '60 minutes ago' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && continue
    rm -rf "$d"
  done
)

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The suites and the gate

POSITIONS.md:110
- P-124 **The specification's examples are a step of the gate, and every one must pass.** `ant testSpecData` runs the examples extracted from `Specification/` under walk (F-114 says which 130 it runs), and the gate fails if any of them fails. When an example fails, the implementation is fixed: the example is not respelled to get around a gap in walk, and no list of examples allowed to fail is kept.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The one library and the compiled checker

POSITIONS.md:61
- P-148 **The checker's speed comes right after its correctness in priority: a rung that changes the compiled checker also makes the change fast.** The rung times the checker before and after its change. It first makes the change correct. Then, in the same rung, it makes the new code fast, without changing which programs the checker accepts or refuses. So no optimization is left to be done by hand after the landing. Why: the checker must stay usable as it grows. Some slowdown is fine, but new checks have made it orders of magnitude slower, so that the checker ran past the time limit of the batch gate's count stage, and rungs could not land. The timing is a smoke test: one run of each tree, to catch a slowdown of several times; a small difference is noise. The `fortress-repo` skill (`compiler.md`, "The checker's time") gives the steps, their commands and what the rung reports.

content.content:
== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

The library, by the symbolic-operator probe's generators on this tree, `python3 -I explorations/perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/known-fixes.py <tree> empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow` ('empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow: 27 edits in 5 files'), taken as written but for the doc comments (decision 1):

# Rung S of climb batch 21: the symbolic operators' library fixes

- problem: the full check of symbolic operators on the base, 191 errors, 54 of them cleared by the known library fixes (F-245; `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/probes/full-check-base.tsv:169`, String's `||` in String's api, one of 40 family sites); rows 585 and 784: `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:785`, `:805`
- spec: two functional methods whose `self` parameters stand at different positions must satisfy the Subtype Rule or the Incompatibility Rule, so no meet can make String's `(a:Any, self)` beside `(self, b:Any)` valid: `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:518-523`
- precedent: juxtaposition's three top-level operators at `(Any, String)`, `(String, String)` and `(String, Any)`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4491-4493` (base `:4476-4478`), api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2525-2527`
- deviation: the `||` of two strings reaches the string objects' own `||` by a `typecase`, where juxtaposition's `(String, String)` calls `a || b`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4461-4466`
- deviation: String's api states `Concatenable`'s and `EmptyString`'s three `||`, which the api did not state, so that the meet's `typecase` reaches them from `FortressLibrary`: `Library/String.fsi:17-19`, `:29-31`
- historical: Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/String.fsi, Library/String.fss, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss

Branch `wip/rung-symbolic-library`, cut from `00f2e1bdc`, seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base21` (the seeding script exited 0; the base build is at `aa5ff2423`, whose code is `00f2e1bdc`'s: `git diff --stat aa5ff2423 00f2e1bdc -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml` lists only files under `explorations/perf-probes/self-type-exclusion/`), pushed. Commits: `c6d57500d` (the walk guard), `34747e082` (the library and the respelled expected failure). The harness refused the worker's write of this file ("Subagents should return findings as text"); its text is the rung's result.

## 1. What changed, and why

The library, by the symbolic-operator probe's generators on this tree, `python3 -I explorations/perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/known-fixes.py <tree> empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow` ('empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow: 27 edits in 5 files'), taken as written but for the doc comments (decision 1):

- **String's four concatenation families (row 585).** `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///` leave String's trait, where each paired `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)` (base `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2496-2522`, `.fss:4398-4443`), and become three top-level operators each, at `(a:Any, b:String)`, `(a:String, b:String)` and `(a:String, b:Any)`, with today's bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2501-2522`, `.fss:4458-4488`). String's abstract `opr ||(self, b:String)` goes too, since beside it the top-level family would mix a function with a functional method at one name, which row 545 refuses. The meet `opr ||(a:String, b:String)` dispatches by `typecase` to `FlatString`'s or `Concatenable`'s own `||`, else `concatAndBalanceIfNecessary` (`.fss:4461-4466`), and String's api now states `Concatenable`'s and `EmptyString`'s three `||` (`Library/String.fsi:17-19`, `:29-31`) so that `FortressLibrary`, which imports `String.{...}`, sees them (F-249). String keeps its other `||` members (`Number`, `Char`, `()`, the tuples; `fsi:2480-2486`) and the prefix `//` and `///`.
- **EmptyString's meet (row 611's library half):** `opr || (self, _:EmptyString): String = self` (`Library/String.fss:318`).
- **`=` (row 784):** `Integral`'s `opr =(self,b:I):Boolean`, bodiless as its other operators, in api and component (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:452`, `.fss:702`), the meet of `Number`'s `=` and `StandardPartialOrder`'s; `ZZ`'s api states the `opr =(self, b: ZZ)` its component declares (`fsi:655`).
- **`|_|` (row 784, review list item 1):** String's api header extends `DelegatedIndexed[\Char,ZZ32\]` as its component does (`fsi:2424` against `.fss:4329`); `Maybe`'s meet `opr |self| : ZZ32` in api and component (`fsi:981`, `.fss:1631`, restating `Condition`'s body at `.fss:1531`); `Float`'s `opr |self|` answers `RR64` where it wrote `Number` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:79`).
- **Maybe's subscript:** the meet `opr [i:ZZ32]:T throws NotFound` in api and component (`fsi:982`, `.fss:1632`, `Condition`'s body).
- **The api's six top-level `Vector` and `Matrix` `+` and `-` (row 784)** leave the api (base `fsi:1654-1661`, `:1764-1771`); the component never defined them.
- **`^` (review list item 3):** `Float`'s meet `opr ^(self, b:RR64):RR64`, the native `Float$Pow` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:158`).
- **Fork 5:** `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss`'s traits `S` and `T` exclude `String` (`:6`, `:9`), so walk loads the program again and the test keeps its subject and its key (section 3).

The doc comments: the generator left the team's `|||` doc comment orphaned inside String's trait in both files, and wrote a rationale comment over the new block. The `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///` comments now stand over the top-level families (`fsi:2501-2522`, `.fss:4458-4488`); String's own `||` comment stays over its remaining `||` members, and the component's long `//` and `///` comments over the prefix forms.

## 2. The tests: the failing run and the passing runs

Its before is the planner's table on this base, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/probes/full-check-base.tsv`, not run again here (POSITIONS, "No re-measuring what the record holds."). **The walk guard**, `ProjectFortress/tests/StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk.fss`: each of the four families with a string on either side and on both, beside a number, a character, `()`, a pair and a triple; `EmptyString` on each side of `||`; that `"ab" || "cd"` is flat, depth 0 (F-249's concern: a meet with `Concatenable`'s body gave a `CatString`); the line separators read through the library's postfix `//` and `///`. data.summary:
Rung S lands the symbolic operators' library fixes by the probe's seven generators, with the team's doc comments moved onto the new declarations. String's four concatenation families, ||, |||, // and ///, are now three top-level operators each, at (Any, String), (String, String) and (String, Any), as juxtaposition's three are. The || of two strings reaches FlatString's or Concatenable's own || by a typecase, and String's api now declares those methods. The rest of the fixes: EmptyString's meet; Integral's and ZZ's =; String's api header extends DelegatedIndexed; Maybe's |self| and subscript meets; Float's |self| answers RR64; Float's ^ meet; and the api's six Vector and Matrix + and - are gone.

The test is the full-check stage, measured against the planner's base table. It went from 191 errors to 137: 54 sites gone and none new. What remains is the 124 subscript sites (rung B), 8 vector sites (rung X), the gate's 5, and the three caught AnyList crash lines. The stock count stays at 3 and the distance at 5, with the same five sites. String's export entry no longer says 'different extends clauses'. The count stage took 95 s.

Under walk, the new guard StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk passes on the base and after the edit. ant testSystem ran 669 tests with 0 failures, and ant testSpecData 130 with 0 failures. The ladder subset and the eighteen microGPT components are unchanged. The one test that moved is XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator: walk now refuses it for String's new top-level || beside the test's own ||. Its traits now exclude String, and it again shows its expected failure under its original key (fork 5). No sentence of the specification's text becomes false. Record sentences that do: F-245, F-81, F-249, F-259, and rows 585, 784 and 611. REPORT.md and record.md were refused by the harness, so their full text is in the result fields.
data.reportText:
# Rung S of climb batch 21: the symbolic operators' library fixes

- problem: the full check of symbolic operators on the base, 191 errors, 54 of them cleared by the known library fixes (F-245; `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/probes/full-check-base.tsv:169`, String's `||` in String's api, one of 40 family sites); rows 585 and 784: `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:785`, `:805`
- spec: two functional methods whose `self` parameters stand at different positions must satisfy the Subtype Rule or the Incompatibility Rule, so no meet can make String's `(a:Any, self)` beside `(self, b:Any)` valid: `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:518-523`
- precedent: juxtaposition's three top-level operators at `(Any, String)`, `(String, String)` and `(String, Any)`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4491-4493` (base `:4476-4478`), api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2525-2527`
- deviation: the `||` of two strings reaches the string objects' own `||` by a `typecase`, where juxtaposition's `(String, String)` calls `a || b`: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4461-4466`
- deviation: String's api states `Concatenable`'s and `EmptyString`'s three `||`, which the api did not state, so that the meet's `typecase` reaches them from `FortressLibrary`: `Library/String.fsi:17-19`, `:29-31`
- historical: Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/String.fsi, Library/String.fss, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss

Branch `wip/rung-symbolic-library`, cut from `00f2e1bdc`, seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base21` (the seeding script exited 0; the base build is at `aa5ff2423`, whose code is `00f2e1bdc`'s: `git diff --stat aa5ff2423 00f2e1bdc -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml` lists only files under `explorations/perf-probes/self-type-exclusion/`), pushed. Commits: `c6d57500d` (the walk guard), `34747e082` (the library and the respelled expected failure). The harness refused the worker's write of this file ("Subagents should return findings as text"); its text is the rung's result.

## 1. What changed, and why

The library, by the symbolic-operator probe's generators on this tree, `python3 -I explorations/perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/known-fixes.py <tree> empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow` ('empty str4 eq abshead maybeidx vecops floatpow: 27 edits in 5 files'), taken as written but for the doc comments (decision 1):

- **String's four concatenation families (row 585).** `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///` leave String's trait, where each paired `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)` (base `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2496-2522`, `.fss:4398-4443`), and become three top-level operators each, at `(a:Any, b:String)`, `(a:String, b:String)` and `(a:String, b:Any)`, with today's bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2501-2522`, `.fss:4458-4488`). String's abstract `opr ||(self, b:String)` goes too, since beside it the top-level family would mix a function with a functional method at one name, which row 545 refuses. The meet `opr ||(a:String, b:String)` dispatches by `typecase` to `FlatString`'s or `Concatenable`'s own `||`, else `concatAndBalanceIfNecessary` (`.fss:4461-4466`), and String's api now states `Concatenable`'s and `EmptyString`'s three `||` (`Library/String.fsi:17-19`, `:29-31`) so that `FortressLibrary`, which imports `String.{...}`, sees them (F-249). String keeps its other `||` members (`Number`, `Char`, `()`, the tuples; `fsi:2480-2486`) and the prefix `//` and `///`.
- **EmptyString's meet (row 611's library half):** `opr || (self, _:EmptyString): String = self` (`Library/String.fss:318`).
- **`=` (row 784):** `Integral`'s `opr =(self,b:I):Boolean`, bodiless as its other operators, in api and component (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:452`, `.fss:702`), the meet of `Number`'s `=` and `StandardPartialOrder`'s; `ZZ`'s api states the `opr =(self, b: ZZ)` its component declares (`fsi:655`).
- **`|_|` (row 784, review list item 1):** String's api header extends `DelegatedIndexed[\Char,ZZ32\]` as its component does (`fsi:2424` against `.fss:4329`); `Maybe`'s meet `opr |self| : ZZ32` in api and component (`fsi:981`, `.fss:1631`, restating `Condition`'s body at `.fss:1531`); `Float`'s `opr |self|` answers `RR64` where it wrote `Number` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:79`).
- **Maybe's subscript:** the meet `opr [i:ZZ32]:T throws NotFound` in api and component (`fsi:982`, `.fss:1632`, `Condition`'s body).
- **The api's six top-level `Vector` and `Matrix` `+` and `-` (row 784)** leave the api (base `fsi:1654-1661`, `:1764-1771`); the component never defined them.
- **`^` (review list item 3):** `Float`'s meet `opr ^(self, b:RR64):RR64`, the native `Float$Pow` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:158`).
- **Fork 5:** `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss`'s traits `S` and `T` exclude `String` (`:6`, `:9`), so walk loads the program again and the test keeps its subject and its key (section 3).

The doc comments: the generator left the team's `|||` doc comment orphaned inside String's trait in both files, and wrote a rationale comment over the new block. The `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///` comments now stand over the top-level families (`fsi:2501-2522`, `.fss:4458-4488`); String's own `||` comment stays over its remaining `||` members, and the component's long `//` and `///` comments over the prefix forms.

## 2. The tests: the failing run and the passing runs

**The full-check stage is the rung's test** (the brief, section S, "Distance sites"; fork 3). Its before is the planner's table on this base, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/probes/full-check-base.tsv`, not run again here (POSITIONS, "No re-measuring what the record holds."). Its lines for String's `||` in String's trait, api and component (`full-check-base.tsv:169`, `:176`):

    overloading	||	same-sparams	api FortressLibrary	overloading	FortressLibrary.fsi:2502,FortressLibrary.fsi:2503	Invalid overloading of || in trait String: (Any, String)->String @ FortressLibrary.fsi:2502:5-30 and (String, Any)->String @ FortressLibrary.fsi:2503:5-2507:82
    overloading	||	same-sparams	component FortressLibrary	overloading	FortressLibrary.fss:4411,FortressLibrary.fss:4412	Invalid overloading of || in trait String: (Any, String)->String @ FortressLibrary.fss:4411:5-50 and (String, Any)->String @ FortressLibrary.fss:4412:5-4416:82

with its total, by the planner's run (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-21.md:122`): '#total 191', '#kind overloading 182', 'return-type 1', 'typecheck 4', 'export 1', 'other/overloading 3'.

The after, once, on the final tree (`34747e082`), started 14:51:31Z:

    explorations/perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/run-shadow.sh tmp/rung-symbolic-library/full-check-postedit.tsv tmp/rung-symbolic-library/fc-post catch
    #total	137
    #kind	overloading	132
    #kind	typecheck	4
    #kind	export	1
    #crash	none
    #seconds	242	FortressLibrary 171

with the three `@@PROBE CRASH` lines of the `AnyList` crash caught, on `||` in `List`'s api and component and `String`'s component ('E is not in the kind env'), as on the base. Compared:

    python3 -I explorations/perf-probes/array-sites/compare-sites.py explorations/compile-ladder/plan-21/probes/full-check-base.tsv tmp/rung-symbolic-library/fc-post/d/errors.tsv
    landed 191 now 137

with 53 `GONE` lines (one of them `x2`), so 54 sites gone, and no site come. Section 4 gives them by family.

**The walk guard**, `ProjectFortress/tests/StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk.fss`: each of the four families with a string on either side and on both, beside a number, a character, `()`, a pair and a triple; `EmptyString` on each side of `||`; that `"ab" || "cd"` is flat, depth 0 (F-249's concern: a meet with `Concatenable`'s body gave a `CatString`); the line separators read through the library's postfix `//` and `///`. It guards behaviour that works, so it has no failing run (`tests-writing.md`, "The order"). On the base's code, before the library edit (14:47:14Z):

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-symbolic-library/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk.fss
    # harness-one 2026-10-23T14:47:14Z; tree 00f2e1bdc; nproc=4; load 0.96 0.77 1.89; openjdk version "25.0.4.1" 2026-08-18; FORTRESS_THREADS=4; cache filled
     OK (time = 3855ms)
    OK (1 test)

It went red with one expected value changed for one run, in a copy under `tmp/` with `"(1,2,3)a"` for `"(1,2,3) a"`: 'Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1'. After the edit (14:50:15Z), in one call with the expected failure:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-symbolic-library/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.test
    . interpret tmp/rung-symbolic-library/h1/tests/StringConcatenationFamiliesWalk 
     OK (time = 10154ms)

and green again in `ant testSystem` (section 8).

## 3. XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator (fork 5)

On the base (14:47:43Z), `harness-one.sh ... XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.test`: 'Vo || 3 = 1', 'Saw expected failure: loaded and ran, not refused at load', 'OK (1 test)'.

With the library edit and the test unchanged (14:50:15Z, the call above), red:

     Refused at load, but did not satisfy load_exception_contains; expected
    Invalid overloading of ||
    com.sun.fortress.exceptions.ProgramError: com.sun.fortress.exceptions.ProgramError: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4467:1-4471:78: and
    tmp/rung-symbolic-library/h1/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss:10:3-33:
    first parameters a:[String,Any] and self:[T,ZZ32] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor equal) and no excluding pair is present

The pair is the library's new `opr ||(a:String, b:Any)` (`.fss:4467`; the span runs on over the doc comment after it) beside the test's `opr ||(self, b: ZZ32)` in trait `T`. By the Meet Rule the refusal is right: `T` and `String` can meet, and no declaration covers `(String & T, ZZ32)`. With the default, `trait S excludes { String }` and `trait T excludes { String }` (14:50:39Z):

    harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-symbolic-library/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.fss ProjectFortress/tests/XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator.test
    Vo || 3 = 1
     Saw expected failure: loaded and ran, not refused at load
    OK (1 test)

The test keeps its subject (an object inheriting two symbolic operators with no meet, which walk's meet check skips: row 611) and its key, `load_exception_contains=Invalid overloading of ||`. The red run above shows that the harness reads the key. The rule this exposes: under walk, a program's own trait with a functional `||`, `|||`, `//` or `///` that can meet `String` now needs `excludes { String }` or a meet. A grep of the walk tests, `test_library/`, the specification's examples, the demos and both microGPT programs for a declaration of one of the four operators (`grep -rln 'opr *\(||\|||| *\|//\|///\) *(' ProjectFortress/tests ProjectFortress/test_library SpecData ProjectFortress/demos explorations/run-c4/src explorations/apl/mg`) prints only this test.

## 4. The stages

**The full check, site by site** (section 2's comparison). Gone, 54, none come:
